claim: PDLIM2 was repressed in over 75% of human lung tumors using 40% of the expression level in matched normal lung tissues as the cut-off.
source: Using 40% of the expression level in matched normal lung tissues as the cut-off in the analysis of the Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) data, we found that PDLIM2 was repressed in over 75% of human lung tumors in a prior study (Sun et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by analysis of TCGA database and cited prior study

claim: PDLIM2 was repressed in about 94% of human lung tumors using 50% as the cut-off.
source: If using 50% as the cut-off, PDLIM2 was repressed in about 94% of human lung tumors (Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by TCGA data analysis shown in Figure 1A

claim: Over 70% of human lung tumors have hypermethylation of the PDLIM2 promoter using 125% of the methylation level in normal lung tissues as the cut-off.
source: Using 125% of the methylation level of the PDLIM2 promoter in normal lung tissues as the cut-off to analyze TCGA database, over 70% of human lung tumors were found to have hypermethylation of the PDLIM2 promoter (Figure 1A and B)
evidence: Supported by TCGA database analysis shown in Figures 1A and 1B

claim: Epigenetic silencing is the main mechanism underlying PDLIM2 repression.
source: over 70% of human lung tumors were found to have hypermethylation of the PDLIM2 promoter (Figure 1A and B), further validating our previous finding of epigenetic silencing as the main mechanism underlying PDLIM2 repression (Sun et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by TCGA data and cited prior study

claim: PDLIM2 is located on chromosome 8p21.3, a frequent LOH region in lung and other tumors.
source: In line with PDLIM2's location on chromosome 8p21.3, a frequent LOH region in lung and other tumors (Wistuba et al., 1999; Kang, 2015; Macartney-Coxson et al., 2008; Swalwell et al., 2002; Wurster et al., 2017)
evidence: Supported by multiple cited references

claim: PDLIM2 expression is positively associated with its gene copy numbers.
source: analysis of TCGA database revealed that PDLIM2 expression was positively associated with its gene copy numbers
evidence: Supported by TCGA database analysis

claim: Over 58% of human lung tumors have genetic deletion of the PDLIM2 gene using CNV of –0.1 as the cut-off.
source: over 58% of human lung tumors had genetic deletion of the PDLIM2 gene if copy number variation (CNV) of –0.1 was used as the cut-off for the gene deletion (Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by TCGA database analysis shown in Figure 1C

claim: About 44% of human lung tumors simultaneously harbor promoter hypermethylation and LOH of the PDLIM2 gene.
source: Further analysis indicated that about 44% of human lung tumors simultaneously harbored the promoter hypermethylation and LOH of the PDLIM2 gene
evidence: Supported by TCGA database analysis

claim: Approximately 27% of human lung tumors have only promoter hypermethylation of the PDLIM2 gene.
source: approximately 27% and 14% of them only having the promoter hypermethylation or LOH of the PDLIM2 gene, respectively (Figure 1D).
evidence: Supported by TCGA database analysis shown in Figure 1D

claim: Approximately 14% of human lung tumors have only LOH of the PDLIM2 gene.
source: approximately 27% and 14% of them only having the promoter hypermethylation or LOH of the PDLIM2 gene, respectively (Figure 1D).
evidence: Supported by TCGA database analysis shown in Figure 1D

claim: Around 15% of lung tumors possess no epigenetic or genetic alterations in PDLIM2.
source: Around 15% of lung tumors possessed no such epigenetic or genetic alterations in PDLIM2.
evidence: Supported by TCGA database analysis

claim: PDLIM2 LOH in human lung tumors was confirmed by microsatellite and gene-specific PCR-based LOH analysis.
source: These findings were confirmed by microsatellite and gene-specific PCR-based LOH analysis of human primary lung tumor tissues and cell lines (Figure 1E and F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1E and 1F

claim: PDLIM2 repression in lung cancer involves both epigenetic silencing and genetic deletion.
source: These data suggested that PDLIM2 repression in lung cancer involves both epigenetic silencing and genetic deletion.
evidence: Inferred from the combined TCGA and experimental data showing both mechanisms

claim: PDLIM2 is detected in the lung of Pdlim2+/- mice at a much lower level compared to wild type mice.
source: Unlike its absolute absence in Pdlim2 homozygous deletion (Pdlim2-/-) mice, PDLIM2 was detected in the lung of Pdlim2+/- mice, but at a much lower level compared to wild type (WT) mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by IHC assays shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A

claim: PDLIM2 is absolutely absent in Pdlim2-/- mice.
source: Unlike its absolute absence in Pdlim2 homozygous deletion (Pdlim2-/-) mice
evidence: Supported by IHC assays shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A

claim: Pdlim2+/- mice develop spontaneous tumors.
source: Importantly, Pdlim2+/- mice, like Pdlim2-/- mice, also developed spontaneous tumors (Figure 1G).
evidence: Supported by Kaplan-Meier survival curve shown in Figure 1G

claim: Pdlim2-/- mice develop spontaneous tumors.
source: Importantly, Pdlim2+/- mice, like Pdlim2-/- mice, also developed spontaneous tumors (Figure 1G).
evidence: Supported by Kaplan-Meier survival curve shown in Figure 1G

claim: Over 50% of tumors developed in Pdlim2-/- and Pdlim2+/- mice are lung tumors.
source: Of note, over 50% of tumors developed in Pdlim2-/- and Pdlim2+/- mice were lung tumors (Figure 1H; Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1H and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B

claim: PDLIM2 is ubiquitously expressed under physiological conditions, with the highest level in the lung and lung epithelial cells in particular.
source: These data are also highly consistent with the fact that PDLIM2 is ubiquitously expressed under physiological conditions, with the highest level in the lung and lung epithelial cells in particular (Sun et al., 2019; Torrado et al., 2004; Tanaka et al., 2005; Loughran et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by multiple cited references

claim: PDLIM2 is a haploinsufficient tumor suppressor that is particularly important for lung tumor suppression.
source: Thus, PDLIM2 is a haploinsufficient tumor suppressor that is particularly important for lung tumor suppression.
evidence: Inferred from the data showing Pdlim2+/- mice develop spontaneous tumors, predominantly lung tumors

claim: PDLIM2 LOH accounts for about 58% of all lung cancer cases.
source: Although reversal of PDLIM2 epigenetic repression by epigenetic drugs to restore PDLIM2 expression in cancer cells may be used to treat lung cancer (Sun et al., 2019), it is logical that this approach cannot be applied to lung tumors involving PDLIM2 LOH, which accounts for about 58% of all lung cancer cases.
evidence: Based on TCGA data analysis showing 58% of lung tumors have PDLIM2 genetic deletion

claim: Urethane is a faithful model of human lung cancer and adenocarcinoma in particular.
source: To this end, we employed mouse lung tumors induced by urethane, a faithful model of human lung cancer and adenocarcinoma (AC) in particular (Sun et al., 2019; Zhou et al., 2015; Qu et al., 2015; Kellar et al., 2015; Zhou et al., 2017; Li et al., 2018; Sun et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by multiple cited references

claim: Urethane is a chemical carcinogen present in fermented food, alcoholic beverage and cigarette smoke.
source: Urethane is a chemical carcinogen present in fermented food, alcoholic beverage and also cigarette smoke, the predominant risk factor accounting for about 90% of human lung cancer cases (Hecht, 2002).
evidence: Supported by cited reference

claim: Cigarette smoke is the predominant risk factor accounting for about 90% of human lung cancer cases.
source: Urethane is a chemical carcinogen present in fermented food, alcoholic beverage and also cigarette smoke, the predominant risk factor accounting for about 90% of human lung cancer cases (Hecht, 2002).
evidence: Supported by cited reference

claim: Murine lung cancer induced by urethane shares PDLIM2 repression with human lung cancer.
source: Like its human counterpart, the murine lung cancer induced by urethane also shares PDLIM2 repression, in addition to their similarities in histology, genetics, molecular biology, and immunology (Sun et al., 2019; Sun et al., 2020; Zhou et al., 2015; Qu et al., 2015; Kellar et al., 2015; Zhou et al., 2017; Li et al., 2018; Sun et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by multiple cited references

claim: NanoPDLIM2-treated mice had a significantly reduced tumor burden in their lungs compared to vector plasmid mock-treated group.
source: Compared to the vector plasmid mock-treated group (Vec), nanoPDLIM2-treated mice had a significantly reduced tumor burden in their lungs, although the decrease in tumor numbers was not statistically significant (Figure 2B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B

claim: The decrease in tumor numbers by nanoPDLIM2 treatment was not statistically significant.
source: Compared to the vector plasmid mock-treated group (Vec), nanoPDLIM2-treated mice had a significantly reduced tumor burden in their lungs, although the decrease in tumor numbers was not statistically significant (Figure 2B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B

claim: NanoPDLIM2 administration decreased nuclear RelA and STAT3 in lung tumors.
source: In line with the tumor reduction, nanoPDLIM2 administration decreased nuclear RelA and STAT3, a hallmark of NF-κB and STAT3 activation
evidence: Supported by IHC staining shown in Figure 2C

claim: Nuclear RelA and STAT3 are hallmarks of NF-κB and STAT3 activation.
source: nanoPDLIM2 administration decreased nuclear RelA and STAT3, a hallmark of NF-κB and STAT3 activation
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge

claim: NanoPDLIM2 reduced the expression of Bcl-xL in lung tumors.
source: accordingly reduced the expression of their downstream cell survival gene Bcl-xL and cell proliferation gene Cyclin D1, increased apoptosis and decreased proliferation of lung cancer cells (Figure 2C-E).
evidence: Supported by IHC staining shown in Figure 2D

claim: Bcl-xL is a downstream cell survival gene of RelA and STAT3.
source: accordingly reduced the expression of their downstream cell survival gene Bcl-xL
evidence: Based on established knowledge of NF-κB and STAT3 signaling pathways

claim: NanoPDLIM2 reduced the expression of Cyclin D1 in lung tumors.
source: accordingly reduced the expression of their downstream cell survival gene Bcl-xL and cell proliferation gene Cyclin D1, increased apoptosis and decreased proliferation of lung cancer cells (Figure 2C-E).
evidence: Supported by IHC staining shown in Figure 2E

claim: Cyclin D1 is a downstream cell proliferation gene of RelA and STAT3.
source: accordingly reduced the expression of their downstream cell survival gene Bcl-xL and cell proliferation gene Cyclin D1
evidence: Based on established knowledge of NF-κB and STAT3 signaling pathways

claim: NanoPDLIM2 increased apoptosis of lung cancer cells.
source: accordingly reduced the expression of their downstream cell survival gene Bcl-xL and cell proliferation gene Cyclin D1, increased apoptosis and decreased proliferation of lung cancer cells (Figure 2C-E).
evidence: Supported by IHC staining shown in Figure 2D

claim: NanoPDLIM2 decreased proliferation of lung cancer cells.
source: accordingly reduced the expression of their downstream cell survival gene Bcl-xL and cell proliferation gene Cyclin D1, increased apoptosis and decreased proliferation of lung cancer cells (Figure 2C-E).
evidence: Supported by IHC staining shown in Figure 2E

claim: Intravenous administration of nanoPDLIM2 shows efficacy in suppressing oncogenic RelA and STAT3 activation in lung cancer.
source: These data indicated that intravenous administration of nanoPDLIM2 shows efficacy in suppressing oncogenic RelA and STAT3 activation and in treating lung cancer.
evidence: Inferred from the experimental data showing decreased nuclear RelA and STAT3

claim: Intravenous administration of nanoPDLIM2 shows efficacy in treating lung cancer.
source: These data indicated that intravenous administration of nanoPDLIM2 shows efficacy in suppressing oncogenic RelA and STAT3 activation and in treating lung cancer.
evidence: Inferred from the experimental data showing tumor reduction

claim: A high level of PDLIM2 was detected in lung tumors from mice treated with PDLIM2 plasmid nanoparticles one week post treatment.
source: Consistent with the treatment efficacy, a high level of PDLIM2 was detected in the lung tumors from mice treated with the PDLIM2 plasmid nanoparticles one week post nanoPDLIM2 treatment, whereas no obvious PDLIM2 was found in the lung tumors from mice treated with the control plasmid nanoparticles (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: Supported by IHC staining and immunoblot shown in Figures 3A and 3B

claim: No obvious PDLIM2 was found in lung tumors from mice treated with control plasmid nanoparticles.
source: a high level of PDLIM2 was detected in the lung tumors from mice treated with the PDLIM2 plasmid nanoparticles one week post nanoPDLIM2 treatment, whereas no obvious PDLIM2 was found in the lung tumors from mice treated with the control plasmid nanoparticles (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: Supported by IHC staining and immunoblot shown in Figures 3A and 3B

claim: The tumor delivery efficiency of PDLIM2-expression or control plasmid nanoparticles was similarly high.
source: It should be pointed out that the tumor delivery efficiency of PDLIM2-expression or control plasmid nanoparticles was similarly high (Figure 3B).
evidence: Supported by PCR data shown in Figure 3B

claim: PDLIM2-expression or control plasmids were hardly detected in liver, kidney and spleen one week after injection.
source: However, either PDLIM2-expression or control plasmids were hardly detected in other organs/tissues of the same mice, including liver, kidney and spleen.
evidence: Supported by PCR data shown in Figure 3B

claim: In the first two days after injection, both empty vector and PDLIM2-expression plasmids were detected at high levels in liver, kidney and spleen but quickly cleared afterward.
source: Of note, in the first two days after injection, both empty vector and PDLIM2-expression plasmids were also detected at high levels in those tissues but quickly cleared afterward (data not shown)
evidence: Supported by experimental data not shown in the manuscript

claim: Nanoparticles show tumor-specific enrichment.
source: consistent with the well-documented tumor-specific enrichment of nanoparticles (Yang et al., 2013; Commisso et al., 2013; Huang et al., 2017; Shi et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by multiple cited references

claim: Ectopic Pdlim2 was not detected in liver, kidney and spleen after nanoPDLIM2 treatment.
source: Consistently, ectopic Pdlim2 was not detected, and the levels of PDLIM2 proteins were comparable in these tissues (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: Supported by immunoblot and IHC data shown in Figures 3B and 3C

claim: The levels of PDLIM2 proteins were comparable in liver, kidney and spleen between PDLIM2-expression and control plasmid nanoparticle treated mice.
source: Consistently, ectopic Pdlim2 was not detected, and the levels of PDLIM2 proteins were comparable in these tissues (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: Supported by immunoblot and IHC data shown in Figures 3B and 3C

claim: I.v. injection of PDLIM2-expression or control plasmid nanoparticles showed no obvious toxicity to animals.
source: In further support of the lung tumor-specific delivery, the i.v. injection of either PDLIM2-expression or control plasmid nanoparticles showed no obvious toxicity to animals, as evidenced by no significant changes in the animal body weight and histology of all organs/tissues we examined, including spleen, kidney and liver (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: Supported by body weight data and H&E staining shown in Figures 3D and 3E

claim: No significant changes in animal body weight were observed after nanoPDLIM2 treatment.
source: the i.v. injection of either PDLIM2-expression or control plasmid nanoparticles showed no obvious toxicity to animals, as evidenced by no significant changes in the animal body weight and histology of all organs/tissues we examined, including spleen, kidney and liver (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: Supported by body weight data shown in Figure 3D

claim: No significant changes in histology of spleen, kidney and liver were observed after nanoPDLIM2 treatment.
source: the i.v. injection of either PDLIM2-expression or control plasmid nanoparticles showed no obvious toxicity to animals, as evidenced by no significant changes in the animal body weight and histology of all organs/tissues we examined, including spleen, kidney and liver (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: Supported by H&E staining shown in Figure 3E

claim: Mouse appearance and behaviors were not different between PDLIM2-expression and control plasmid nanoparticle groups.
source: Mouse appearance and behaviors, such as eating, drinking, defecating, urinating, sniffing, grooming, and digging, were not different between PDLIM2-expression and control plasmid nanoparticle groups (data not shown).
evidence: Supported by observational data not shown in the manuscript

claim: PDLIM2-based nanotherapy shows therapeutic efficacy and low toxicity in the mouse model of refractory lung cancer.
source: Taken together, these data suggested the therapeutic efficacy and low toxicity of PDLIM2-based nanotherapy in the mouse model of refractory lung cancer.
evidence: Inferred from the combined data showing tumor reduction and lack of toxicity

claim: PDLIM2 inhibits the expression of cell survival and proliferation genes in tumor cells, which contribute to chemoresistance.
source: Given the role of PDLIM2 in inhibiting the expression of cell survival and proliferation genes in tumor cells, which contribute to chemoresistance
evidence: Based on prior studies and data showing PDLIM2 effects on Bcl-xL and Cyclin D1

claim: Treatment with carboplatin and paclitaxel led to significant decrease in tumor number and tumor burden.
source: Treatment with carboplatin and paclitaxel, two chemotherapeutic drugs that are often used together as the first-line treatment for lung and many other cancers, led to significant decrease in tumor number and tumor burden (Figure 4A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A

claim: Carboplatin and paclitaxel are often used together as the first-line treatment for lung and many other cancers.
source: Treatment with carboplatin and paclitaxel, two chemotherapeutic drugs that are often used together as the first-line treatment for lung and many other cancers
evidence: Based on established clinical practice

claim: Combination of nanoPDLIM2 with chemotherapy further significantly decreased both tumor number and tumor burden.
source: Importantly, combination with nanoPDLIM2 further significantly decreased both tumor number and tumor burden, suggesting a promising synergy between PDLIM2 nanotherapy and chemotherapy in lung cancer treatment.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A

claim: There is a promising synergy between PDLIM2 nanotherapy and chemotherapy in lung cancer treatment.
source: Importantly, combination with nanoPDLIM2 further significantly decreased both tumor number and tumor burden, suggesting a promising synergy between PDLIM2 nanotherapy and chemotherapy in lung cancer treatment.
evidence: Inferred from the experimental data showing enhanced efficacy of combination treatment

claim: Significantly higher tumor cell apoptosis was detected in mice treated with the combination therapy compared to nanoPDLIM2 or chemotherapy alone.
source: Consistently, significantly higher tumor cell apoptosis was detected in mice treated with the combination therapy, in comparison to those with nanoPDLIM2 or chemotherapy alone (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by IHC staining shown in Figure 4B

claim: Chemotherapy induced strong RelA activation/nuclear expression.
source: Chemotherapy induced strong RelA activation/nuclear expression and MDR1 expression (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: Supported by IHC staining shown in Figure 4C

claim: Chemotherapy induced MDR1 expression.
source: Chemotherapy induced strong RelA activation/nuclear expression and MDR1 expression (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: Supported by IHC staining shown in Figure 4D

claim: NanoPDLIM2 repressed the constitutive activation of RelA in cancer cells.
source: NanoPDLIM2 not only repressed the constitutive activation of RelA in cancer cells but also prevented the strong induction of RelA activation and MDR1 expression by the chemotherapy.
evidence: Supported by IHC staining shown in Figure 4C

claim: NanoPDLIM2 prevented the strong induction of RelA activation by chemotherapy.
source: NanoPDLIM2 not only repressed the constitutive activation of RelA in cancer cells but also prevented the strong induction of RelA activation and MDR1 expression by the chemotherapy.
evidence: Supported by IHC staining shown in Figure 4C

claim: NanoPDLIM2 prevented the induction of MDR1 expression by chemotherapy.
source: NanoPDLIM2 not only repressed the constitutive activation of RelA in cancer cells but also prevented the strong induction of RelA activation and MDR1 expression by the chemotherapy.

claim: PDLIM2 nanotherapy improves the therapeutic efficacy of chemotherapy through blocking both intrinsic and acquired chemoresistance of lung cancer cells.
source: Thus, PDLIM2 nanotherapy improves the therapeutic efficacy of chemotherapy through blocking both intrinsic and acquired chemoresistance of lung cancer cells.

claim: High expression of cell survival genes renders tumor cells resistant to the tumoricidal activity of cytotoxic T lymphocytes.
source: High expression of cell survival genes also renders tumor cells resistant to the tumoricidal activity of cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs), including those unleashed by ICIs.

claim: PDLIM2 nanotherapy should enhance the efficacy of immunotherapy given its ability in suppressing the expression of cell survival genes.
source: PDLIM2 nanotherapy should also enhance the efficacy of immunotherapy, given its ability in suppressing the expression of cell survival genes.
evidence: Speculative reasoning based on PDLIM2's known effects

claim: NanoPDLIM2 increased the expression of MHC-I.

claim: TILs and MHC-I are the most important and core components of immunotherapies including PD-1 immune checkpoint blockade therapy.

claim: PD-1 blocking antibody showed some efficacies in the mouse model of lung cancer.
